scoring_justification: Main artifact (step02) reports computed frequencies/energy compared against paper-reported experimental values with tolerances; recomputing DFT is infeasible. Geometry is audited structurally.

hidden_assets.purpose: Reference values for vibrational frequencies, red-shifts, subgap energy, and gas-phase frequencies
hidden_assets.source_provenance: Paper: Fig. 1(c) experimental IR peak positions (1389, 1524 cm-1), calculated red-shifts (86, 92 cm-1), subgap energy ~0.4 eV above VBM; gas-phase hydride frequencies from Ref. 21 used as reference for shifts.
hidden_assets.generation_method: Values extracted from the published paper and reproduce the computational result the paper reports.
hidden_assets.why_not_fabricated: Numbers directly trace to the paper's reported experimental observations and computational analysis; they are not invented.

schema.description: XYZ file: first line number of atoms, second line comment with hydrogen labeling (Ht/Hd), then element_symbol x y z (Å).

outputs.description: Relaxed atomic geometry after DFT optimization. The checker performs a structural audit: verifies that exactly two hydrogen atoms are present, one has trigonal coordination to In, Ga, Zn, and the other has twofold coordination to Ga, Zn, within a distance cutoff of 2.5 Å.

Computed vibrational and electronic properties. The checker compares the M-H stretching frequencies, red-shifts, and subgap energy against hidden reference values derived from the experimental data, with appropriate tolerances.
